name: Standard Scramble

waypoints.name: West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trailhead (Trail #411)
waypoints.note: Vault toilet and stock loading ramp at the trailhead; a Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park, and Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness rules apply once you enter the wilderness boundary.
waypoints.directions: From Twisp, follow the Twisp River Road about 10.7 miles and turn left onto Buttermilk Creek Road, crossing the Twisp River. Stay left onto East Buttermilk Road (Forest Road 43) and follow it roughly 4 miles, then turn right onto the Road 500 spur and follow it about 2.7 miles to the West Fork Buttermilk Creek trailhead at about 3,960 ft. There is a vault toilet and a stock loading ramp at the trailhead; a Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park, and Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness rules apply once you cross the boundary on Trail #411.

waypoints.name: West Fork Buttermilk Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Creek crossing has been rerouted to a downed log about 100 ft upstream of the original ford after trail damage; last easy, reliable water for several miles.
waypoints.directions: Follow Trail #411 up the West Fork Buttermilk Creek valley about a mile to the crossing of the West Fork. In high water look for the downed-log crossing about 100 ft upstream of the original ford; this is the last easy, reliable water for several miles.

waypoints.name: Sub-alpine larch stand below Fish Creek Pass
waypoints.note: Trail breaks out of burned forest into the lowest larches on the route, roughly two miles below the pass; open going but watch for deadfall from the old burn.
waypoints.directions: Continue up Trail #411 through the old burn, where long stretches of blowdown interrupt the tread and further fords of the West Fork come early in the season, until the trail breaks out into the lowest larches at about 6,800 ft.

waypoints.name: Fish Creek Pass
waypoints.note: High point of the maintained trail (Trail #411 tops out here); first clear view down to Star Lake and the Star Peak massif opens up.
waypoints.directions: Keep climbing through open larch country to Fish Creek Pass at 7,480 ft, the high point of the trail and the first clear view of Star Lake and the Star Peak massif.

waypoints.name: Star Lake
waypoints.note: Standard basecamp for Star, Courtney, Buttermilk, Grey, and Oval Peaks; camp at least 200 ft from the lake edge per wilderness regulation.
waypoints.directions: From the pass the trail drops slightly for about half a mile into the Star Lake basin at about 7,460 ft. Camp at least 200 ft from the lakeshore.

waypoints.name: Notch west of Point 7912
waypoints.note: Climber's path switchbacks up terrible scree from the Star Lake basin to this notch; from here the route turns north onto Star Peak's west/SW ridge.
waypoints.directions: Pick up the climber's path out of the basin and follow it as it switchbacks about 600 ft up steep, loose scree to the notch just west of Point 7912; the rocky point beside the notch confirms it is the right one. If snow still fills the bowl the path vanishes, so navigate to the notch.

waypoints.name: SW ridge talus and scree slog
waypoints.note: Extended rock-hopping through large, unstable talus to gain the summit ridge; not technical but tedious and twisted-ankle terrain, worse if wet or snow-covered.
waypoints.directions: From the notch, turn onto the peak's southwest ridge, where broken blocky rock and sandy patches replace the scree, and rock-hop through large, unstable talus. Stay on or near the established line rather than dropping into the steeper loose gullies below it.

waypoints.name: Star Peak
waypoints.note: True summit and high point of Sawtooth Ridge; easy scrambling with hands and feet on the final approach, broad views across the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.
waypoints.directions: Follow the ridge to the summit, with a little easy hands-and-feet scrambling on the final approach. Descend the same line; do not shortcut down the unstable boulder field on the peak's east side.

approach: Trailhead is the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trailhead (Trail #411), reached via Twisp River Road ~10.7-10.8 miles from Twisp, then left on Buttermilk Creek Road, staying left onto East Buttermilk Road (Forest Road 43) for roughly 4 miles, then right onto the Road 500 spur for about 2.7 miles to the road-end trailhead at about 3,960 ft. From there Trail #411 climbs the West Fork Buttermilk Creek drainage into the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness. Tread is inconsistently maintained in the lower-to-mid section — parties describe long stretches of blowdown with only brief clear tread, so plan to navigate by map/GPS rather than blazes. Several fords of the West Fork are the main early-season hazard: in June/early summer with high runoff these crossings can be genuinely difficult, sometimes requiring a detour upstream to find a log crossing. About 2 miles before Star Lake the trail enters the lowest larches, and roughly a half mile before the lake it crests Fish Creek Pass, an open viewpoint over the larch-covered Sawtooth Range and a good landmark/rest stop with reliable water nearby. From the pass, the trail drops slightly into the Star Lake basin (~7,460 ft) — 7.5 miles and about 3,500 ft of gain from the trailhead. Snow commonly lingers on the upper approach slopes into summer (encountered from roughly 6,000 ft up in early-season conditions), so a light axe/spikes are worth carrying outside of late-season. From Star Lake, pick up a climber's trail heading up into the bowl south of the lake, contour around Point 7912, and gain the SW ridge; a steep, loose scree track leads from the basin up to the ridge crest. From there it's scree-walking, talus-hopping, and some easy Class 2-3 hands-and-feet scrambling along the ridge east to the 8,693 ft summit. Total one-way distance from trailhead to summit runs roughly 8.5-9 miles with about 4,730 ft of cumulative gain. An alternate approach uses the Lady of the Lake ferry from Chelan to Prince Creek Landing, then climbs North Fork Prince Creek to the Sawtooth crest and reaches Star Peak via Star Pass — the classic way to combine it with Courtney Peak and other Sawtooth summits.

itinerary.cal: The West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail is brushy and poorly maintained in its upper miles; most parties go mid-July through early October once snow clears from the Fish Creek Pass area and larches aren't yet the draw until late September/early October.

days.note: Hike the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail up to Star Lake, the standard basecamp for Star Peak. The trail is steep and increasingly brushy/poorly maintained in its upper miles, so this is a slower 7.5-mile carry than the mileage alone suggests. Camp at least 200 ft from the lakeshore per wilderness rules.
days.title: Backpack in to Star Lake basecamp

days.note: Drop the overnight pack and go light: up the scree bowl south of the lake to the pass, contour around point 7912, then follow the SW ridge east to the summit. It's technically easy but slow, loose scree/talus travel with some easy hands-and-feet scrambling near the top. Strong parties often tag Courtney and/or Oval Peak from the same camp, but this plan covers Star Peak alone.
days.title: Summit day: Star Peak

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack, cross to the bowl south of Star Lake.

schedule.label: Top of scree bowl / pass
schedule.detail: Gain the pass at the head of the bowl (waypoint S2 on the standard route).

schedule.label: Contour around Pt. 7912
schedule.detail: Climber's trail traverses below the point rather than going over it.

schedule.label: Gain the SW ridge
schedule.detail: Follow the ridge, then trend east for the final scramble to the summit.

schedule.label: Summit (8,693 ft)
schedule.detail: Views across the Sawtooth/Lake Chelan wilderness; typical summit stay 20-30 min.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the route; rest, or use remaining daylight for Courtney/Oval if energy allows.

days.objective: Climb Star Peak (8,693 ft) from Star Lake camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse Day 1's route back down to the trailhead. Mostly downhill but the same brushy, sometimes hard-to-follow tread makes it slower going than a groomed trail of this length.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the West Fork Buttermilk Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~18.6-mile backpack trip (one night in, one summit day, one night out) that lines up with the 4,730 ft gain / 18.6 mi round trip; very fit parties have pushed it car-to-car in a single ~18-20 hour day, but that's an outlier, not the recommended plan.

approach_variants.name: West Fork Buttermilk to Star Lake
approach_variants.notes: Seven and a half miles of trail from the West Fork Buttermilk road end to Star Lake, and the tread is inconsistently maintained through the middle of it — long stretches of blowdown with only brief clear sections, so navigate by map or track rather than by looking for tread. Several fords of the West Fork are the main early-season problem and can force a detour upstream to find a log. Two miles below the lake the trail enters the lowest larches, and half a mile before it the trail crests Fish Creek Pass, an open viewpoint with water nearby and the first clear look at the peak. The lake basin is the standard camp and also serves several neighbouring summits. A boat-in approach from Lake Chelan up Prince Creek reaches the same crest from the other side.
approach_variants.season: Mid-July to early October; larch Sep
hazards: Large, deeply unstable talus at the base of the summit block
Rockfall onto anyone below on the loose scree track, worst on descent
Off-trail route-finding above the lake, including a contour that is easy to lose in snow
Afternoon thunderstorms and lightning on a wholly open ridge
High fords early in the season
Long and remote with minimal cell coverage
approach_variants.baseFinding: From Star Lake the peak stands north across the basin, and the base of the scramble is a notch on the ridge just west of a rocky point about 600 ft above the lake. Pick up the climber's path leaving the basin south and southeast of the lake and follow it as it switchbacks up genuinely poor scree to that notch; the point immediately east of the notch is Point 7,912, and it is the landmark that tells you the notch is the right one. From the notch the route turns north onto the peak's west and southwest ridge, and the ground changes character at once: broken blocky rock and sandy patches instead of running scree. Stay on or near the established contour rather than dropping into the steeper loose gullies below it, which look like shortcuts and are not. Above this the ridge is talus-hopping with occasional hands-on moves. If snow is still lying in the bowl the path disappears entirely, and the notch beside the point is what you navigate to.
